Nikhil / team — ran the capacity sweep and a quick ops feasibility pass. Summary below (ops note):

Inventory snapshot (US regions):
- Available A100-80GB equiv (dedicated poolable units): 18 nodes convertible to dedicated instances across us-west-2 and us-east-1 within target window.
- Contention window: high demand for mid-Jan due to Q1 onboarding from other large deals; recommend confirming by Dec 10th to keep the pool listable.

Recommended approach (soft embargo):
1) Soft-embargo window: 60 days starting on customer's requested start date. During embargo we mark 12 units as "standby-dedicated" in our scheduler (preventing new on-demand assignments but not billing the customer until activation).
2) Release policy: automatic release 7 days after requested start if activation handshake not completed; extension requests require AE approval.
3) Fallback: if actual capacity shortfall occurs at activation we offer: (a) spill to compatible spot-backed nodes + graceful degraded model (quantized variant) for up to 14 days; (b) cross-region failover to the alternate region within 24-48h (customer pays data egress).
4) Ops requirements from VeloxAI: signed intent (simple form), expected activation window (72h accuracy), and workload p95/p99 tail latencies under 2s in the attached profile to validate fit.

Constraints & caveats:
- The hold reduces flexibility for other enterprise commitments; we can only maintain the soft-embargo if sales approvals are in by Dec 10.
- If customer requires strict billing for reserved capacity (commit), we need finance procurement lanes and 30-day lead to provision isolated VPC onboarding.

Attachments: estimated-sprint-flags.xlsx (cost delta scenarios), runbook-soft-embargo.pdf (ops steps + activation checklist).

If this structure looks good I can draft the 1-page runbook for procurement and a short SLA-oriented paragraph for the contract team.

-ben
